thread.title: UPDATE: Apple earnings: Watch these 4 numbers

author: morningstar.com
title: UPDATE: Apple earnings: Watch these 4 numbers
text:
By Emily Bary
China revenue, average selling price can help show underlying strength of the business
Apple Inc.'s iPhone unit sales are generally the main focus of the smartphone giant's earnings reports, but this quarter might be different.
Since Apple (AAPL) is due to release its next iPhone lineup in the next few months, investors may be less concerned with how many iPhones people are buying now (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/apple-earnings-most-boring-quarter-of-the-year-still-holds-some-intrigue-2018-07-27) and rather more interested in whether underlying trends remain strong at Apple. Here are the key numbers to watch when Apple reports results Tuesday afternoon.
Live coverage: Apple earnings will be all about the forecast (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/apple-earnings-will-be-all-about-the-forecast-live-blog-2018-07-31)
September outlook
The most important data point in the June-quarter report will likely concern the September quarter.
With the next iPhone on investors' minds, the biggest hint Apple might provide on its conference call about the forthcoming device could come in its forecast for the current quarter. Apple typically launches new iPhones in the fall, but its phones don't always go on sale during the September quarter. Thus, if Apple delivers a somewhat higher-than-expected outlook for the September period, that could suggest the company expects at least some of its new phones to come out during the period.
Currently, analysts surveyed by FactSet project $59.5 billion in revenue for the September quarter.
Don't miss: Here's how much Apple could make from streaming (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/how-much-could-apple-make-from-original-video-content-2018-06-25)
It's worth noting that the forecast Apple issued a year ago ended up pleasing investors, who saw it as a sign that the company didn't expect delays (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/apple-earnings-calm-iphone-fears-send-stock-to-record-levels-2017-08-01) with its then-upcoming iPhone line. In the end, Apple's iPhone 8 and 8 Plus came out in time to count in the September quarter, but its flagship iPhone X didn't launch until November (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/apple-earnings-iphone-x-supply-is-the-question-but-the-answer-may-not-matter-2017-10-30).
For investors tempted to look farther ahead, Bernstein analyst Toni Sacconaghi wrote last week that Apple's September quarter outlook has historically " *not* been a helpful predictor of the strength of the forthcoming cycle," while the company's gross-margin forecast for the period "has only been helpful when Apple has guided meaningfully lower."
Services revenue
An increasingly important part of Apple's business is its fast-growing services segment (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/apple-earnings-show-iphone-supercycle-isnt-happening-and-thats-ok-2018-02-01), which includes Apple Music, iCloud, and the App Store. For the June quarter, analysts tracked by FactSet project $9.2 billion in services revenue, up from $7.3 billion a year ago. That would amount to a 26% growth rate.
"While services grew an eye-popping 31% in the March quarter, we acknowledge that pace is unlikely to be sustainable," wrote CFRA analyst Angelo Zino. He projects that services revenue will grow 28% in the quarter.
Cascend Securities analyst Eric Ross wrote Tuesday that Apple Music could account for almost $800 million in June-quarter revenue, though he expects that the service has lower margins than those offered by Spotify Technology SA (SPOT) or Pandora Media Inc. (P) (Pandora is also on Tuesday's earnings docket (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/pandora-earnings-a-new-member-of-the-band-could-matter-beyond-the-music-2018-07-27).)
Apple doesn't break out services revenue by subsection, but it will be worth watching for commentary on Apple Music as well as the App Store.
Average selling prices
With the next iPhone cycle so close, iPhone sales are less of a focus these days (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/apple-earnings-most-boring-quarter-of-the-year-still-holds-some-intrigue-2018-07-27) than they normally are. Pay attention to a related metric, however, for a sign of how much consumers are generally willing to pay for phones. Apple's average selling price is a decent indicator of the mix behind higher- and lower-priced iPhones, as well as whether consumers are experiencing fatigue due to Apple's high prices.
Analysts surveyed by FactSet project that the iPhone commanded an average selling price of $693 during the quarter, up from $606 in the year-earlier period but down from $728 in the March quarter. The June quarter tends to be the lowest quarter seasonally in terms of average selling price.
China
China revenue is a closely watched but hotly debated element of Apple's business. Greater China sales have been on the upswing (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/the-surprise-in-apple-earnings-big-growth-in-china-2018-05-01) for Apple lately after a period of weakness, but analysts want to know the source of the turnaround. Watch for commentary on whether unit sales in China remain strong, or whether other areas are driving China strength. The services business is likely getting a nice lift in China, and watches could also be helping matters somewhat.
-Emily Bary;
